st.3: Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa describes the rise of Chandragupta Maurya against the Nandas.

x: All three statements are correct: Vishakhadatta wrote both plays, the Devichandraguptam tells of Ramagupta and Chandragupta II, and the Mudrarakshasa covers Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya against the Nandas.

st.3: The Orientalists wanted the grant spent exclusively on Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning, with no Western subjects.
st.1: H.T. Colebrooke and James Mill were in the Orientalist camp.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Munro backed vernacular schooling in Madras. Statement 1 is wrong – James Mill was an Anglicist (Colebrooke and H.H. Wilson were Orientalists); statement 2 is wrong – Trevelyan was an Anglicist; statement 3 is wrong – the Orientalists accepted some Western subjects alongside classical learning.

st.2: The Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Dayal Singh, a former Brahmo.
st.3: The Dev Samaj stressed the eternity of the soul and the supremacy of the guru, but did not forbid alcohol or meat.
st.4: The Bharat Dharma Mahamandal was a body of orthodox Hindus with its headquarters later at Lahore.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 – the Dharma Sabha opposed the abolition of sati; statement 2 – the Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri (Shiv Dayal Singh founded the Radhasoami Satsang); statement 3 – the Dev Samaj forbade alcohol and meat; statement 4 – the Mahamandal's headquarters was at Varanasi (Lahore was the Dev Samaj's base).

st.3: The Neolithic painting at Velpulamadugu shows humped bulls facing each other.

x: All three statements are correct: the Borra Caves were found in 1807 by William King, the Ketavaram Mesolithic paintings are in Kurnool, and Velpulamadugu shows humped bulls facing each other.

st.2: The Arjuna ratha is the largest and a forerunner of the Dravida vimana.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong – the Dharmaraja ratha is the largest; statement 4 is wrong – the Draupadi ratha, not the Bhima, is the smallest hut-shaped cell.

st.2: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was split off in 1999.

x: All three statements are correct: the Ministry of Welfare (1985) became Social Justice and Empowerment in 1998, Tribal Affairs was split off in 1999, and Minority Affairs was carved out on 29 January 2006.

st.1: It is called the 'Mini Constitution' because it changed the Preamble, the Eighth Schedule and 53 Articles.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: it added the Fundamental Duties as Part IVA. Statement 1 is wrong – it changed the Seventh Schedule, not the Eighth; statement 3 is wrong – it curtailed but did not abolish judicial review.

st.4: Social security is a first-generation right.
st.1: René Cassin proposed the three-generation classification in 1977.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: third-generation rights are linked with fraternity. Statement 1 is wrong – Karel Vasak proposed the classification (1977); statement 3 is wrong – eradication of social discrimination is not a first-generation right; statement 4 is wrong – social security is a second-generation right.

st.4: In 2024-25, Vijayawada was named a 'Promising Swachh Shehar' in the 10 lakh+ category.
st.1: In 2022, Guntur was the 'Top Impact Creator' in the million-plus category.
st.3: In 2023, Vijayawada ranked 4th in India and was AP's cleanest city.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 – the 2022 'Top Impact Creator' was Visakhapatnam; statement 2 – Tirupati was 1st in 'Safaimitra Suraksha Shehar' (Vijayawada was the cleanest capital); statement 3 – in 2023 Visakhapatnam was 4th and AP's cleanest; statement 4 – Vijayawada entered the Super Swachh League (Rajahmundry was the Promising Swachh Shehar).

st.2: e-PDS supplies food grains to all families, including non-BPL ones, through fair price shops.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 – there are 29,796 Fair Price Shops (9,260 was the number of Mobile Dispensing Units); statement 2 – e-PDS supplies food grains to BPL families; statement 3 – door delivery was discontinued on 1 May 2025.

st.3: The Bahamas' Sand Dollar (2020) was the world's first live retail CBDC.

x: All three statements are correct: the wholesale e-rupee pilot began on 1 November 2022, the retail pilot on 1 December 2022, and the Bahamas' Sand Dollar (2020) was the first live retail CBDC.

st.3: In joint cooperative farming, produce is shared according to both the land and the labour contributed.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kumarappa Committee (1949) recommended cooperative farming, the Nagpur Resolution (1959) made it a goal, and in joint cooperative farming produce is shared by land and labour contributed.

st.3: In ODOP-2024 AP won the State Award and all the District Awards.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: AP ranked 17th in the Fiscal Health Index 2023-24. Statement 1 is wrong – Rushikonda holds the Blue Flag; statement 3 is wrong – AP won 10 of the 12 District Awards, not all of them.

st.4: It is calculated by the full market capitalisation method.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: it is managed by NSE Indices Ltd. Statement 1 is wrong – it was launched on 22 April 1996 (1 January 1986 is the SENSEX); statement 2 is wrong – its base value is 1000; statement 4 is wrong – it uses the free-float method.

st.2: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

x: All three statements are correct: Ceres is the largest asteroid-belt body, the belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, and a comet's tail points away from the Sun.

st.3: The Chambal ravines are an example of gully erosion.

x: All three statements are correct: weathering is the first stage and deposition the last, running water leads except in arid areas like the Thar where wind leads, and the Chambal ravines show gully erosion.

st.3: Tropical evergreen forests, receiving 100–200 cm of seasonal rain, are also called monsoon forests.
st.2: The Congo Basin has the largest tropical rainforest in the world.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: teak and sal shed their leaves in the dry season. Statement 1 is wrong – rainforests get over 200 cm; statement 2 is wrong – the Congo Basin is the second-largest (the Amazon is the largest); statement 3 is wrong – the monsoon forests are the tropical deciduous forests.

st.2: 5G Standalone (SA) does not depend on a 4G core network.

x: All three statements are correct: Sanchar Saathi and ASTR are fraud tools, 5G SA runs independently of the 4G core, and the Bharat 6G Vision targets 2030.

st.3: NRSC's CROP framework estimated rabi 2024-25 wheat production at 122.724 MT.

x: All three statements are correct: the FASAL expansion is right, MNCFC (2012) runs it, and the CROP framework put rabi 2024-25 wheat at 122.724 MT.

st.2: The only viable population of the Hangul is in Kanha National Park.
st.3: The Nilgiri marten and the Malabar spiny dormouse are found in the Nallamala hills.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Great Indian Hornbill is the state bird of Arunachal Pradesh and Kerala. Statement 2 is wrong – the Hangul's only viable population is in Dachigam NP; statement 3 is wrong – they are Western Ghats (Agasthyamalai) species; statement 4 is wrong – Podocarpus wallichianus is the only endemic gymnosperm of the Western Ghats.

st.1: It has raised about Rs 120 crore since 2008.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Red Sanders accounts for about 45%. Statement 1 is wrong – ABS has raised over Rs 266 crore (Rs 120 crore is the Red Sanders share); statement 3 is wrong – 25–40% goes to the repository and 60–75% to local communities.

st.3: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence for two generations (50 years).

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong – the nodal ministry is Tribal Affairs; statement 3 is wrong – OTFDs need three generations (75 years) of residence.

st.2: Installed solar capacity was 117 GW in September 2023.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: India was third after China and the USA. Statement 2 is wrong – the 117 GW mark was in September 2025; statement 3 is wrong – parity with coal came around 2017.

st.1: It was established in 1997 by the Bangkok Declaration and has its headquarters in Dhaka.

x: All three statements are correct: BIMSTEC was set up in 1997 by the Bangkok Declaration with headquarters in Dhaka, its 6th Summit was at Bangkok on 4 April 2025, and Bhutan and Nepal are members but the Maldives is not.

st.3: Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana lead the States in services-sector employment.

x: All three statements are correct: services give over 55% of GVA but under one-third of jobs, their employment share was 29.7% in 2023–24, and Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana lead the States.

st.2: A commemorative postage stamp and a ₹75 coin were released.

x: All three statements are correct: it marked 1,000 years since January 1026 and 75 years since May 1951, a stamp and a ₹75 coin were released, and the theme was "Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi".

st.3: National Girl Child Day (24 January) was launched in 2008 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

x: All three statements are correct: National Voters' Day marks the ECI's founding on 25 January 1950, the first was observed in 2011, and National Girl Child Day was launched in 2008.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh marked the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology with the Visakhapatnam Quantum Valley.
st.2: As per PLFS 2017-18, 76.95% of rural women work in agriculture.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 – AP's initiative is the Amaravati Quantum Valley; statement 2 – the 76.95% figure is from PLFS 2023-24; statement 3 – 2025 was the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, not Renewable Energy.

st.1: The repo rate was kept unchanged at 5.25%, having last been cut by 25 bps in June 2025.
st.4: The policy stance has been accommodative since June 2025.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the CRR stood at 3% of NDTL. Statement 1 is wrong – the last 25 bps cut was in December 2025; statement 3 is wrong – the hold was unanimous; statement 4 is wrong – the stance has been neutral since June 2025.

st.1: It provides a 90-day pause in peak sowing and harvest seasons.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 – the pause is 60 days; statement 2 – allocation is normative, set by the Centre (the bottom-up labour budget was the MGNREGA method).

st.1: It was launched in Vijayawada on Independence Day, 15 August 2026.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: World Population Day was set up in 1989 by UNDP. Statement 1 is wrong – it was launched on World Population Day, 11 July 2026 (15 August was only the earlier expected start); statement 2 is wrong – the fourth child gets ₹40,000.

st.2: The State Data Centre will come up at the IIIT Tirupati campus on the BOOT model.

x: All three statements are correct: the AI Living Labs Foundation is a Section-8 company at Amaravati, the State Data Centre is at IIIT Tirupati on the BOOT model, and house regularisation was extended to 30 June 2026.
